Container.Name: rclone-serve
Container.Overview: A fully self-contained rclone appliance: rclone's own official web GUI for guided remote setup (OAuth flows for OneDrive/Google Drive/Dropbox/etc. included) plus `rclone serve` to expose a configured remote over a protocol other tools already speak - most usefully restic's own REST backend - so restic can talk to a cloud provider it has no native driver for directly, without a separate scheduled sync job in between. Owns its own config entirely; no dependency on any other rclone install.
Container.Requires: Nothing pre-existing - point Config Path at an empty directory and configure your first remote through the web GUI after starting the container.

Config.Name: GUI Port
Config.Description: Port for rclone's own web GUI (guided remote setup)

Config.Name: Config Path
Config.Description: Where this container's own rclone.conf and settings are stored - independent of any other rclone install

Config.Name: GUI User
Config.Description: Basic auth username for the config GUI - this is full control over your remotes' credentials

Config.Name: GUI Password
Config.Description: Basic auth password for the config GUI

Config.Name: Remote
Config.Description: The remote:path to serve, e.g. onedrive:backups - doesn't need to exist yet, just needs to be created eventually via the GUI

Config.Name: Serve User
Config.Description: Basic auth username for the serve endpoint

Config.Name: Serve Password
Config.Description: Basic auth password for the serve endpoint

Config.Name: Serve Protocol
Config.Description: restic, http, webdav, or sftp only - other rclone serve modes lack a compatible auth model and are rejected

Config.Name: Extra Args
Config.Description: Extra flags passed straight through to rclone serve
